prose: The 1893 Chicago World's Fair is a cornerstone of the Tartaria and mudflood theory: the claim that its Greco-Roman buildings were dug out of a buried advanced civilization and passed off as new. I believed it for years, until I looked at the historical records and 700 archival photos.

Chance and Dylan dig into the 1893 Chicago World's Columbian Exposition, the cornerstone of the Tartaria and mudflood theory that an advanced lost civilization built the "White City" and that elites faked its construction. Using C.D. Arnold's 700-photo construction archive, period engineering journals, and a frame-by-frame forensic analysis of the so-called impossible photos, this Inner Whirled investigation walks through how the fair was really built with staff plaster, timber, and 40,000 workers, why the "no blueprints" and "no materials" claims collapse on contact with the archive, and what this means for Tartaria.
